concept.title: AI Features
concept.shortdesc: DitaCraft integrates GitHub Copilot and other LLM providers to assist with DITA map restructuring, error explanation, element analysis, and content reuse discovery.

section.title: Overview
section.p: DitaCraft's AI features connect to an LLM provider — GitHub Copilot by default — and layer context-aware DITA intelligence on top of plain chat. All AI commands use the current document's DITA context (topic hierarchy, key space, validation diagnostics), not just raw text.

ol.li: GitHub Copilot — integrated; no API key required when Copilot is installed.
Anthropic (Claude) — requires an API key stored via DitaCraft: Configure AI.
OpenAI (GPT-4o) — requires an API key stored via DitaCraft: Configure AI.
Ollama — local inference; requires Ollama running on localhost:11434 and ditacraft.ai.provider.ollama.enabled set to true.

section.p: Use DitaCraft: Configure AI from the Command Palette to view provider status and store API keys securely via VS Code SecretStorage.

section.title: Configure AI
section.p: Run Command PaletteDitaCraft: Configure AI to open the AI Settings panel.

ul.li: Live status for each provider (available / not configured / unavailable)
Input fields for Anthropic and OpenAI API keys. Keys are stored in VS Code SecretStorage (OS keychain integration) — never in plain-text settings or workspace files.
AI mode selector (auto, copilot-only, byok-only, or local-only)

section.note: With auto mode (the default), DitaCraft tries each provider in priority order and falls back automatically if one is unavailable.

section.title: @ditacraft Chat Participant

dd.p: Proposes a restructured DITA map based on a plain-language intention.

p.codeph: @ditacraft /restructure Group topics by audience: admin first, then end user

dd.p: DitaCraft builds a DITA context snapshot from the active .ditamap, sends it to the LLM, and streams back valid DITA XML. The response is validated by the LSP before being presented. The active tab must be a .ditamap file.
Explains a DITA validation diagnostic at the cursor position in plain language.

p.codeph: @ditacraft /validate why does DITA require unique IDs?

dd.p: DitaCraft reads the first diagnostic on the current line, includes the surrounding XML context, and asks the LLM to explain the error and suggest a fix. If no diagnostics are present, the response confirms the file is valid.
Explains the semantic structure and purpose of the selected DITA element.

Select an XML element in the editor before running this command. The selection is sent to the LLM inside a code fence; any focus instruction you provide is sent separately as context (not embedded inside the XML).
Identifies content reuse opportunities in the current DITA map using conref and keyref patterns.
DitaCraft analyzes the map structure and topic content, then returns a list of concrete reuse suggestions with code examples. The active tab must be a .ditamap file.

section.title: F2: Restructure Map Command
section.p: The DitaCraft: Restructure Map with AI command provides a full diff-and-apply workflow for restructuring a DITA map.

ol.li: Open a .ditamap file (it must be the active tab).
Open the Command Palette and run DitaCraft: Restructure Map with AI. Alternatively, right-click the file in the Explorer and choose Restructure Map with AI.
Enter your restructuring intention in the InputBox that appears.
DitaCraft opens a diff editor showing the current map (left) and the proposed restructure (right).
A dialog asks Apply restructured map? — click Apply to save or Cancel to discard.

section.p: All original href attributes are preserved. The change is undoable with Ctrl+Z.

section.title: F3: AI Quick Fix
section.p: For supported diagnostic codes, DitaCraft offers an ✨ Fix with DitaCraft AI code action alongside the built-in quick fixes.
To use: click the lightbulb icon or press Ctrl+. on a flagged element, then select ✨ Fix with DitaCraft AI.

strow.stentry: Missing or broken href target file
Missing required attribute or structural violation

section.note: The AI quick fix is context-aware: it reads the surrounding XML before proposing the fix, so the result respects your content model.

section.title: F4: AI Completion
section.p: When ditacraft.ai.completion.enabled is true (default), DitaCraft appends AI-suggested elements to the standard LSP completion list.

AI completions are identified by the (AI) suffix and the DitaCraft AI detail label. They appear below the native LSP completions (sorted last). The AI suggestion is generated with a 500 ms timeout budget — if the LLM does not respond in time, only native completions are shown.
To disable AI completions, set ditacraft.ai.completion.enabled to false in Settings.

section.title: Resilience and Fallback
section.p: DitaCraft uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when an LLM provider is unavailable:

ul.li: After 3 consecutive failures within 5 minutes, the provider's circuit opens and no further calls are attempted for 10 minutes.
After the cooldown, one probe request is sent (HALF_OPEN state). If it succeeds, the circuit closes; if not, the cooldown resets.
Cancelled requests (user pressed Escape) do not count as failures.

section.p: When the active provider's circuit is open, DitaCraft automatically falls back to the next available provider in the cascade (Copilot → Anthropic → OpenAI → Ollama).

section.title: Metrics and Telemetry
section.p: When ditacraft.ai.telemetry.enabled is true, DitaCraft logs AI call metrics to the DitaCraft output channel in the format:
Each line shows: command name, provider used, latency in milliseconds, and estimated token count. Failed calls show ✘ instead of ✔.
Metrics are retained in memory (capped at 1,000 entries) and cleared on extension restart. They are never sent to any remote service.

section.title: AI Settings Reference

strow.stentry: Provider cascade mode: auto, copilot-only, byok-only (Anthropic or OpenAI only), or local-only (Ollama only)
Show AI-suggested completions alongside LSP completions
Base URL for the Ollama server
Log AI call metrics (provider, latency, tokens) to the output channel

section.note: Setting ditacraft.ai.mode to local-only while ditacraft.ai.provider.ollama.enabled is false will produce a configuration conflict error on startup. Use byok-only if you want to use only your Anthropic or OpenAI key without Copilot or Ollama.
